info.title: CRM API
info.description:
Everything here is under `/api`. Replace the host with wherever you run the server (default `http://127.0.0.1:3000`).

## Quick start

```sh
# 1. First run only: create the admin account (this also signs you in via cookie)
curl -c jar -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"email":"me@example.com","password":"a-long-password"}' http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/auth/register

# 2. Make an API key. The key is shown once.
curl -b jar -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name":"scripts"}' http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/api-keys

# 3. Use the key
export KEY=crm_...
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name":"Companies"}' http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/tables
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Stage","type":"select","options":[{"label":"Lead"},{"label":"Won"}]}' http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/tables/Companies/fields
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"values":{"Name":"Acme","Stage":"Lead"}}' http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/tables/Companies/records
```

To try calls on this page, click **Authorize** and paste an API key, or sign in to the app in this browser first (the session cookie is used automatically).

## Model

There are no built-in objects. You create **tables**, add typed **fields**, and write **records**. A table URL segment accepts the table's name or ID. Record `values` accept field names (case-insensitive) or field IDs. Every table has one primary text field, `Name`.

A record looks like `{"id", "created_at", "updated_at", "created_by", "updated_by", "values": {...}}`. Writes send `{"values": {...}}`; `POST` sets the listed fields and `PATCH` changes only the listed fields. `null` clears a field. Unknown keys are rejected.

## Value formats

| Field type | JSON value |
|---|---|
| text | string, up to 100,000 characters |
| number | number; whole numbers only if the field has `config.integer` |
| boolean | `true` / `false` |
| date | `YYYY-MM-DD`, or a date-time such as `2026-03-01T09:30:00Z` |
| phone | international number; spaces, dashes, dots and parentheses are stripped; stored as E.164 (`+14155552671`) |
| select | option label or ID on write; the label on read |
| multi_select | array of option labels or IDs on write; array of labels on read |
| relation (to one) | record ID string, or `null`; the target record must exist |
| relation (to many) | array of record IDs (no duplicates, at most 1000) |

## Filters

The `filter` query parameter is URL-encoded JSON. A condition is `{"field", "op", "value"}`. Groups are `{"and": [...]}` and `{"or": [...]}`, nested up to 8 levels, 50 conditions in total.

```json
{"and": [
  {"field": "Stage", "op": "eq", "value": "Won"},
  {"or": [
    {"field": "Amount", "op": "gt", "value": 100},
    {"field": "Owner", "op": "is_empty"}
  ]}
]}
```

Operators by field type:

| Type | Operators |
|---|---|
| text, phone | `eq`, `neq`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `in`, `is_empty`, `is_not_empty` |
| number, date | `eq`, `neq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `in`, `is_empty`, `is_not_empty` |
| boolean | `eq`, `neq`, `is_empty`, `is_not_empty` |
| select, relation (to one) | `eq`, `neq`, `in`, `is_empty`, `is_not_empty` |
| multi_select, relation (to many) | `has`, `has_any`, `is_empty`, `is_not_empty` |

`in` and `has_any` take an array. System columns can be filtered and sorted as `$id`, `$created_at`, `$updated_at`, `$created_by`, `$updated_by`.

Example: `GET /api/tables/Companies/records?filter=%7B%22field%22%3A%22Stage%22%2C%22op%22%3A%22eq%22%2C%22value%22%3A%22Won%22%7D`

## Pagination

`limit` is 1 to 200 (default 50). Follow `next_cursor` until it is `null`. A cursor works only with the same `filter` and `sort`.

## Errors

Failures return `{"error": {"code", "message"}}` with status 400, 401, 403, 404 or 409.

get.description: True while the database has no users. Use it to choose between register and login.

post.description: Works only while no user exists. The first user becomes admin and is signed in. Afterwards it returns 403; an admin creates accounts with `POST /api/users`.
Sets the `crm_session` cookie. Scripts should use an API key instead (see `POST /api/api-keys`).
Admin only. There is no email sending, so give the person the temporary password yourself.

patch.description: Admin only. Change the password or the admin flag. The last admin cannot be demoted.

delete.description: Admin only. The last admin cannot be deleted.

get.description: The key value is never shown again after creation.

post.description: The response holds the key itself. Save it now; only a hash is stored. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
Creates a real SQLite table with a primary text field named `Name`.

get.summary: Get a table with its fields

delete.description: Soft delete: the data stays in the database, but the table disappears from the API.

post.description: Adds a column (or a join table for multi-select and to-many relations).

patch.summary: Rename a field or change its options
patch.description: Type and config cannot change. For select and multi-select, `options` replaces the list: send existing options with their `id` to keep them. Options left out are removed.

delete.description: The primary field cannot be deleted.

get.description: Returns one page. Follow `next_cursor` until it is `null`.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: URL-encoded JSON filter tree. See the Filters section above.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: URL-encoded JSON array of `{field, dir}`, at most 5 keys. Not allowed on relation or multi-select fields.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` from the previous page. Use it only with the same filter and sort.

post.description: Fields you leave out stay empty. Unknown keys are rejected.

patch.description: Changes only the listed fields. `null` clears a field.

get.description: Full-text search. Results are grouped by table, best match first. Tables with no match are left out.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search text. The last word matches as a prefix.

post.description: Config may name fields; the server stores IDs, so renames keep working.

patch.description: `config` replaces the old config. `kind` cannot change.

id.description: Set when keeping or editing an existing option.

table.description: Relation fields: target table name or ID.

many.description: Relation fields: link to many records. Default false.

values.description: Field name (case-insensitive) or field ID -> value. See Value formats above.

filter.description: Same filter tree as the records `filter` parameter.

stale.description: True when the config names a field or option that no longer exists.

sessionCookie.name: crm_session
sessionCookie.description: Set by login or register. Browsers send it automatically.
